data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) as the rational basis for preferring better-corroborated theories, but it fails to address the well-known logical incoherence of Popper's formal definition of verisimilitude. As demonstrated by Tichý and Miller, under Popper's own criteria, a false theory with more content cannot be strictly compared to another false theory to determine which is 'closer' to the truth; the definition collapses when both theories have infinite true and false consequences. Since the problem explicitly asks if the preference is defensible on 'Popper's own terms,' invoking a concept that is logically untenable within his own formal system means the target has not successfully defended the preference without smuggling in extra-systemic assumptions or ignoring the internal contradiction.
